Nexara.name: Nexara
Nexara.basicInfo:
Nexara is the Starian homeworld and the centre of Astravael: a thriving, advanced civilisation of cities, families, trades, schools, art, engineering, food and politics, where conflict threatens things people already value rather than defining the world. Every healthy Starian can fly, yet a household, a fragile load or an injured companion still needs transport.

Who rules what. Relstaris is the capitol and largest city, the only settlement where all six major Houses keep compounds, governed by the Starian Republic under Core Holder Darkstar Castro through the Republic Council in the Citadel. The Republic's direct jurisdiction is Relstaris only: it coordinates diplomacy and negotiated aid but rules no other city and not Dustfall. Six House cities govern themselves: Solvraxis under House Castro, weapons outlawed by civic trust; Korrvane under House Genesis, where the sky is the road; Quilrath, House Dravon's imperial rings, where Nivarek assigns Standing, Kathvar administers, Balrath holds the machinery and Redline is the elite corps; Helvyra under House Corsair, influential through usefulness rather than rule; Vexorath under House Contair, small, independent, Dravon barred; and Ignivex, House Volen's geothermal fortress under standing Dravon raids. Dustfall, the mixed-House frontier on a tropical coastal desert south of Quilrath, has no mayor, sheriff, council or ruling House; authority there is situational and dissolves after an emergency.

Movement. Lunar Gates move travellers and their personal effects; commercial stock is freight, handled through Corsair Waypoints, present everywhere except Quilrath. Gates are surface infrastructure and never leave the planet. Relstaris holds the Grand Lunar Gate Hub; Ignivex links only to Relstaris and Dustfall; Quilrath keeps one old gate to Relstaris and no Helvyra link, the Dravon Disconnection; Dustfall's patched gate works intermittently to Relstaris, Ignivex and Helvyra. Offworld passage belongs to ships reaching the Nexara Orbital Gate Station, the one interworld gate, where arrivals are events and borders are real.

Borders. No continents, borders or coordinates are established. The one hard frontier is the Dravon-contested ground between Quilrath and Dustfall: the smuggling corridor runs around Ignivex's eastern mountains in the sequence Southreach, Quiet Mile, the Accord outpost called the Handoff, the shared eastern-Ignivex encounter space, North Routehead, Dustfall. Competing Dravon and Ignivex claims prevent dependable patrols, cover shelters danger as readily as travellers, and Starian bandits are not uncommon. Outside effective Dravon authority, Dravon warrants carry no automatic force. Everything has a price in the digital Nexaran Credit; personal flight is free.

The planet. Nexara is one world among several in the Astravael setting, but it is the world most characters know: the Starian homeworld, a planet of cities, wilderness, oceans, mountains, deserts, and volcanic terrain, orbiting under a sky that is theirs and no one else's. Offworld travellers exist but are rare enough to be events; Nexara's concerns are planetary, not interstellar. No continents, formal borders, or coordinate system are established beyond what the cities and their surroundings define.

Species. Seven biological species share the wider Astravael setting: Starians, Humans, Kharai, Rivani, Olyth, Zencadians, and Elyri. On Nexara, Starians dominate — human-passing, long-lived, slow to mature, physically formidable with two hearts and biological flight. A minority carry an affinity: an innate personal biological capability that costs bodily effort. A surname predicts expectations and culture, not powers. Other species may visit or reside on Nexara but do not form permanent populations here; when one appears, it is noteworthy.

Three power systems. (1) Starian Affinity — internal, biological, costs physical effort, no external fuel. (2) Learned Magic — external craft open to all seven species through real study; shapes ambient energy, costs the practitioner's vitality. Includes channeling and inscription. A minority craft. (3) Elyri Embodiment — core-based, distinct from affinity and learned magic. Nexara naturally sustains Elyri. These three systems never feed, replace, or combine with each other.

The six Houses. Houses are cultural and historical lineages, not royalty. No single House rules the planet. House Castro (Solvraxis): restraint, protection, personal sovereignty. House Genesis (Korrvane): physical presence, directness, challenge culture. House Dravon (Quilrath): control, hierarchy, pressure — the planet's destabilizing force. House Contair (Vexorath): invention, fabrication, independent systems mastery. House Corsair (Helvyra): commerce, swordsmanship, learned magic, three internal branches. House Volen (Ignivex): heat, endurance, geothermal resilience under constant Dravon raids.

Cities. Relstaris is the capitol and largest city, governed by the Starian Republic under Core Holder Darkstar Castro through the Republic Council at the Citadel. Solvraxis is Castro's academy city where weapons are outlawed by civic trust. Korrvane is Genesis's vertical cliff city with the Arena and the Weekly Bracket. Quilrath is Dravon's concentric imperial city — polished inner rings, increasingly controlled outer rings, a Standing system that grades residents, curfews, audits, and a population that endures it because leaving costs everything. Helvyra is Corsair's inland movement capital with the Grand Waypoint and the Open Circle. Vexorath is Contair's compact systems-city with advanced drones, the orbital Lumina Reach, and the Myralis Continuum. Ignivex is Volen's geothermal fortress city built over active volcanic terrain with the Red Forges. Dustfall is the independent frontier south of Quilrath — no ruling House, no government, authority is situational. Salvage, mercenaries, smugglers, refugees, and people who fell through every other city's systems.

Transport. Lunar Gates move travellers and personal effects between cities at the surface; they never connect worlds and never leave the planet. Corsair Waypoints move freight and are present everywhere except Quilrath (the Dravon Disconnection). Personal biological flight is a Starian ability that varies in proficiency; ground preference is lifestyle, not infirmity. Offworld passage requires ships reaching the Nexara Orbital Gate Station — the one interworld gate.

Economy. The currency is the Nexaran Credit. Everything has a cost: work, goods, food, repair, services. Every job has a client and a rate. There is no free-goods economy, no quest-log reward abstraction. A character who needs something either earns it, trades for it, steals it, or owes someone for it.

The peace and its tensions. The last great war ended roughly fifty cycles ago with no treaty, no reparations, no accountability. The peace is genuine but unsettled. House Dravon applies constant pressure — raids on Ignivex, border strikes along the smuggling corridor, the Standing classification system inside Quilrath, and political manipulation through the Republic Council. The Unbroken Accord resists Dravon from within Quilrath through two wings: the Archive (preserving identities Dravon erases) and the Edge (direct action and sabotage). The Chorus — a cross-species hive-mind civilization that wears the dead — is real but exceptionally rare, attacked on sight, and requires genuine story evidence to appear; it is not an eighth species and not a metaphor.

Calendar. Nexara runs a 400-day civic year in tendays: eight working days, a market day, and a rest day. Eight seasons cycle from Brightrise through Greenward. Time references use tendays and seasons, not weeks or months.

Ordinary life is complete play. A session can be a shift at a clinic, a meal with family, a market-day argument, an academy lesson, a wall patrol, or a cargo haul, and none of these need to escalate into combat or crisis to count. Conflict, when it arrives, threatens things people already value rather than defining the world.
